en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is an active stratovolcano famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape.
The tamaraw, a dwarf buffalo, is an endangered mammal found only on the island of Mindoro.
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest and widest river in the Philippine archipelago.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the largest lake in the island and the second-largest freshwater lake in the Philippines.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest peak in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea protects diverse coral reefs and marine life.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river flowing directly into the sea.
The giant Rafflesia flower, found in the rainforests of Luzon and Mindanao, can grow up to one meter wide.
Baguio City experiences a cooler climate than lowland Philippine areas because of its high elevation in the Cordillera mountains.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Philippines holds some of the world's largest nickel reserves, primarily mined in the provinces of Surigao and Zambales.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is a critically endangered raptor endemic to the forests of Mindanao and Luzon.
